newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen A shares end down sharply on crackdown.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen A shares end down sharply on crackdown.

text.p: Shenzhen's A share index dived on Friday on heavy selling triggered by an warning by the China Securities Regulatory Commission of a crackdown on excessive speculation in the stock market, brokers said.

The A share index plunged 17.24 points, or 4.33 percent, to 380.61, after hitting an intraday low of 371.88. Turnover was 11.52 billion yuan compared with 13.23 billion on Thursday. The composite index fell 15.55 points or 4.20 percent to 354.51.
The B share index was little affected, inching down 0.34 points, or 0.37 percent, to 90.85 on turnover of HK$14.71 million, compared with HK$15.26 million.

China's top securities watchdog said in a notice in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times that there had been excessive speculation and manipulation in the stock market and anyone guilty of it would face a severe penalty.

This triggered heavy profit-taking in the A share market, especially in third-liners that had risen steeply on speculative demand over the past sessions, brokers said. The A share index had surged more than 200 percent since April this year.
Investor confidence was severely dented by the day's sharp decline and the market needs time to consolidate, brokers said.
But a modest rebound may be seen early next week due to Friday's steep drop, brokers said.
Chemical fibre maker Kunshan Sanshan, the worst performer, tumbled 1.10 yuan, or 9.95 percent, to 9.95 yuan.

Conglomerate Zhonghao slumped 1.09 yuan, or 9.61 percent, to 10.25 yuan and floppy disk maker Huayuan slid 0.97 yuan, or 9.35 percent, to 9.40 yuan. Hainan-based pharmaceutical issue Haiyao bucked the trend on institutional support, rising 1.05 yuan, or 8.43 percent, to 13.50 yuan, brokers said.
B shares moved in a narrow range in dull trade, brokers said.
Beverage maker Shenbao was the worst performing share on speculative selling, brokers said. It dipped HK$0.20, or 8.33 percent, to HK$2.20 on thin trade of 6,200 shares.
Building materials producer Fangda fell on profit-taking, down HK$0.19, or 4.20 percent, to HK$4.33 as 261,000 shares changed hands, brokers said.
Dadonghai traded the most on volume of 983,300 shares and edged up HK$0.01 to HK$1.33. It has been the focus of trading by institutions interested in its cheap price, brokers said.
China Merchants, the second most active counter, firmed HK$0.02 to HK$3.40 on higher volume of 552,500 shares.
